definitions.explanation: An affectionate and casual way to address or refer to one's older brother.

definitions.gloss: young man; big brother (to a stranger)
definitions.explanation: Used by children to address an unfamiliar young man in a friendly way.

examples.japanese: お{兄|にい}ちゃん、{遊|あそ}ぼう。
お{兄|にい}ちゃんは{今|いま}{大学|だいがく}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: My big brother is going to college now.

examples.japanese: お{兄|にい}ちゃんがいると{心強|こころづよ}い。
examples.english: Having a big brother is reassuring.

examples.japanese: お{兄|にい}ちゃん、{風船|ふうせん}とって。
examples.english: Mister, get my balloon for me.

examples.japanese: {知|し}らない{子|こ}にお{兄|にい}ちゃんと{呼|よ}ばれた。
examples.english: A child I didn't know called me 'big brother.'

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}で{小|ちい}さい{子|こ}に「お{兄|にい}ちゃん、{一緒|いっしょ}にサッカーしよう」と{言|い}われた。
examples.english: A little kid at the park said to me, 'Hey mister, let's play soccer together.'

notes:
The most casual and affectionate way to say "older brother." Primarily used by younger siblings, especially children. The お prefix and ちゃん suffix together create a warm, familiar tone.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- お{兄|にい}ちゃん: casual, affectionate (children and close family)
- お{兄|にい}さん: standard polite form
- {兄|あに}: humble form used when speaking about one's own brother to outsiders
- {兄貴|あにき}: informal, used among young men; sometimes used toward non-family

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{兄|にい}ちゃんっ{子|こ}: a child who adores their older brother
- お{兄|にい}ちゃん{大好|だいす}き: I love my big brother

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{兄|にい}さん: older brother (polite) — more formal than お{兄|にい}ちゃん
- {兄|あに}: older brother (humble) — used in formal speech about one's own brother
- お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん: older sister (affectionate) — the female counterpart
